candidates.title: Ancient Egypt Unveiled: Treasures from Egyptian Museums
candidates.blurb: Egyptian state collections travel to Hong Kong, testing how pharaonic artefacts read in a museum built for Qing aesthetics.

candidates.title: Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed
candidates.blurb: The Met's jewellery trove shown in a city where ornament still signals social currency, not just historical curiosity.
candidates.why_shortlisted: resonance with local culture of adornment

candidates.title: Wonders of Imperial Carpets: Masterpieces from the Museum of Islamic Art, Doha
candidates.blurb: Islamic carpets from Doha face Qing silks, a trans-regional conversation on courtly luxury through textiles.

candidates.title: The Adorned Body: French Fashion and Jewellery 1770–1910 from the Musée des Arts Décoratifs, Paris
candidates.blurb: Rococo to Belle Époque fashion staged where East-West aesthetic trade has always been transactional, not theoretical.

candidates.title: A History of China in Silk: The Chris Hall Collection at the Hong Kong Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: A Western collector's silk archive becomes institutional, raising questions about whose expertise canonises Chinese textile history.

candidates.title: Alicja Kwade: Waiting Pavilions
candidates.blurb: Kwade's stone-and-mirror pavilions occupy a former prison yard, collapsing colonial architecture into cosmological speculation.

candidates.title: Tai Kwun Neon Connection
candidates.blurb: Permanent neon installation in a heritage complex, reframing local signage as material culture rather than nostalgia bait.

candidates.title: Proudly from Canton: The Muwen Tang Collection of Cantonese and Export Art
candidates.blurb: Export painting and Cantonese craft from a single collection, mapping how Pearl River Delta aesthetics shaped global taste.
candidates.why_shortlisted: regional art history with trade implications

candidates.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice
candidates.blurb: Hong Kong's Venice Biennale collateral shown at home, a feedback loop between international art-world positioning and local reception.

candidates.title: Live: Hong Kong Art Exhibition
candidates.blurb: A survey of Hong Kong art with a title suggesting urgency or documentation, worth watching for what gets canonised.

candidates.title: Wu Guanzhong Art Sponsorship Cross-disciplinary Series: Light Entry
candidates.blurb: Cross-disciplinary response to Wu Guanzhong's work, testing how Hong Kong's most institutionalised modernist still prompts new thinking.
